claims.statement: GHK-Cu is indexed by PubChem as CID 133697840 and associated with CAS number 300801-03-0.

extractedEvidence.quote: Prezatide is a tripeptide consisting of glycine, histidine, and lysine which readily forms a complex with copper ions.
Prezatide is used in cosmetic products for the skin and hair.

reviewFlags: verify aliases and CAS across product types

independent review: DrugBank entry DB11296 ('Prezatide') corroborates the Gly-His-Lys copper-complex identity and cosmetic-use context; DrugBank's own CAS field was login-gated so CAS 300801-03-0 was cross-confirmed via vendor chemical-safety listings (e.g. Cayman Chemical, MedKoo) rather than a second free structured-database CAS field — flagged for a future stronger CAS cross-check

claims.statement: A review describes GHK-Cu research in skin regeneration and wound-healing contexts, with substantial preclinical evidence and cosmetic/topical relevance; BioStack should keep topical/cosmetic claims separate from injectable or systemic claims.

extractedEvidence.quote: Wound healing activity of GHK-Cu was confirmed in animal experiments
Topical GHK-Cu Gel for Acute Skin Wound Healing (CuHeal)

reviewFlags: do not generalize topical evidence to injectable/systemic use

independent review: an independently registered Phase 2 controlled human trial (CuHeal, ctv-cuheal-trial) is testing topical GHK-Cu gel vs. placebo gel on standardized punch-biopsy wounds in adults; as of the accessed date the trial is enrolling with results pending — human efficacy is NOT yet established, so 'substantial preclinical evidence' in this claim must not be read to imply proven human efficacy

claims.statement: BioStack should separate GHK-Cu topical/cosmetic evidence from broad anti-aging, systemic healing, or injectable wellness claims unless source-specific human evidence supports those exact claims. As of the live FDA 503A bulk drug substances nomination record, GHK-Cu has no FDA drug approval and is not on the 503A bulk drug substances list: its Category 1 nomination was withdrawn (removal from Category 1 announced April 2026) and PCAC consultation on its status is not scheduled until before the end of February 2027. Any vendor or marketing claim that injectable or compounded GHK-Cu is FDA-sanctioned or legitimately compounded under an approved bulk-substance listing is false as of the accessed date.

context.useCase: route and marketing-claim boundary; regulatory status of injectable/compounded GHK-Cu

extractedEvidence.quote: Additionally, the FDA is removing one peptide, GHK-Cu, from Category 1 (substances under evaluation that have not been identified as presenting significant safety risks and as to which FDA is exercising enforcement discretion) for the same reason — withdrawal of the nomination — with PCAC consultation planned before the end of February 2027.

reviewFlags: vendor injectable claims require misinformation monitoring
marked fieldAuthorityRequired=true: claim discusses injectable/regulatory boundary and safety-relevant vendor claims per extraction rules

independent review: live FDA/PCAC 503A nomination record (Orrick regulatory analysis, April 2026) confirms GHK-Cu is not on the 503A bulk drug substances list, its Category 1 nomination was withdrawn, and PCAC review is not scheduled until before Feb 2027 — regulatory gap now stated explicitly rather than left implicit

reviewReasons: Pilot misinformation-heavy evidence packet requires human review before publication.

Regulatory gap: GHK-Cu's Category 1 FDA 503A bulk drug substances nomination was withdrawn (removal announced April 2026) and it is not currently on the 503A bulk drug substances list; PCAC consultation on its status is not scheduled until before the end of February 2027 (source: orrick-fda-pcac-2026). This is now stated in claim ghk-cu-hype-boundary-001 (fieldAuthorityRequired=true) but remains human-review gated pending confirmation of any subsequent PCAC action.

Identity claim ghk-cu-identity-pubchem-001: DrugBank's own CAS number field is login-gated, so CAS 300801-03-0 is corroborated only via vendor chemical-safety-data listings rather than a second free structured-database CAS field — a stronger independent CAS cross-check (e.g. CAS Common Chemistry or ChemIDplus) remains an open item.
